newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's ARS talks of rough gem export quota.
newsitem.headline: Russia's ARS talks of rough gem export quota.

text.p: Russia's Almazy Rossii-Sakha (ARS) monopoly diamond producer said on Tuesday that the Industry Ministry was developing proposals for quotas on the volumes of Russian rough diamonds available for export.

"The (Industry) Ministry will make proposals on setting quotas on the export of natural, uncut rough gems, as well as on their supply volumes to the internal Russian market," said an ARS press release signed by company spokesman Valentin Logunov. ARS is the partner to De Beers in a stalled gem deal.

The release said that ARS, also known by its shortened name AlRos, had signed a cooperation agreement with the ministry in which the latter would help to boost production of both rough and cut, polished diamonds.
It said the agreement would help ARS "to strengthen the position of Russian producers of rough and polished diamonds on world markets".
The ministry would also help ARS develop new gem deposits in Russia while retaining a one-channel system of domestic sales.

"In accordance with the agreement, the Industry Ministry, with the participation of the company, obliges itself to conduct a state policy in the field of the mining, production, use, processing and export of precious stones, as well as investments in this sphere," the statement said.
